items.summary: Installed with a single pip command, one agent operates macOS, Windows and Linux desktops, your own Chrome, a real terminal, and iPhone or Android devices. It locates interface elements through the accessibility tree plus OCR instead of guessing pixel coordinates, supports 48 models across 9 providers, sends no telemetry, and can be driven remotely from Telegram.
items.title: AutoCua: one agent drives your desktop, browser, terminal and phone (MIT, shown on Hacker News Nov 4)

items.summary: Open source under Apache-2.0, the whole stack runs on your own hardware with Docker Compose. Each bot keeps its own conversations, memory and Markdown-written routines, works through a browser, terminal and graphical desktop, and can hand tasks to peer bots or short-lived subagents. Desktop and iOS/Android apps are available, and it connects to your own model keys, Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions, or local models such as Ollama.
items.title: Rakazo: self-hosted platform for persistent AI teammates, v0.8.0 released Nov 4

items.summary: An open-source Apache-2.0 Android calendar app. Once the phone and computer are paired over Wi-Fi or Tailscale with a pinned-certificate HTTPS connection, assistants such as Codex, Claude and Cursor can read, create, change and delete events on the calendars you choose, with no Google account or subscription. It is an early release: the APK is still dev-signed and there is no HTTP MCP gateway yet.
items.title: Sunlith: coding agents on your computer edit your phone calendar over Tailscale (shown on Hacker News Nov 5)
